feed.title: Checked against source
feed.subtitle: Write-ups where a claim is taken to the point where it could have failed. Bitcoin Core, MCP servers, hardware-backed keys.

entry.title: Kubernetes The Hard Way starts at lab 01. This is chapter zero.
entry.summary: The tutorial asks for four Debian 12 machines and says nothing about where they come from. Five ways a cloud image refuses to boot on a real host, and the RAM the thirteen labs actually need — 768 MiB, not the 2048 in the spec.

entry.title: A comparison that cannot fail is not a check
entry.summary: A comment in a Bitcoin Core test file cites a URL that redirects instead of 404ing. Establishing that the replacement holds the same 64 vectors took four independent supports — and two negative controls to show the comparison could fail at all.

entry.title: What MCP servers actually expose
entry.summary: Which tools a server puts in tools/list, read line by line across six codebases. Includes the survey I got wrong and why.

entry.title: git-crypt + Trezor: keeping your repo key off the disk entirely
entry.summary: Wiring git-crypt's GPG mode through trezor-agent, so the repo key is never on the host. With the PIN-matrix mechanics explained and the unlock UX measured.

entry.title: Trezor as a TOTP vault: 2FA codes that never touch disk in plaintext
entry.summary: Encrypting TOTP secrets with the device's own CipherKeyValue, so only ciphertext is stored.

entry.title: Recovering a Trezor GPG identity from a seed phrase, no hardware needed
entry.summary: Deterministic reconstruction of the GPG identity from BIP39 via SLIP-0010, checked against the official test vector. Answers trezor-agent#335.
